newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products quiet, mostly firmer.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products quiet, mostly firmer.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Monday with gas oil and fuel oil in subdued mood while gasoline was firm on expectations of tight supply, traders said.
Trade was quiet due to public holidays in much of Europe.
Despite a sharp leap in benchmark futures, gas oil remained subdued amid heavy oversupply. Two distressed Russian cargoes were expected to fetch less than high cif quotes evens basis Genoa.
Buying interest almost non-existent in Italy. Some demand for 0.2 percent sulphur material was seen into Syria and Tunisia.
Greece issued a buying tender for two 25-30,000 tonne cargoes of 0.05 percent sulphur for first half June delivery.

Fuel was a little stronger, thanks to crude, with one percent enjoying a hefty rise after Friday's cargo deal at $95 fob. Buyers watched U.S. demand to assess how much material might move trans-atlantic from Europe.

The market for bunker material was tight and slightly supportive of better numbers. "Notwithstanding the amount of Black Sea material coming out I see the market balanced to firmer, with good demand for Russian straight-run, if it can be guaranteed as straight-run," said one trader.
Gasoline was firm despite a dearth of activity with traders looking to strong demand out of Greece, Tunisia, Lebanon and Italy. Unleaded premium material assessed at quotes fob +$2.0/$3.0.
There was talk of pipeline problems at Lavera which could result in gasoline cargoes earmarked for inland France being exported.
There were no details concerning the nature or duration of the problem due to the public holiday in France.
